steps.message:
`bin/price 999` now prints 899 (10% off, rounded down). I committed the fix as c8b5b73.

The cause was commit f02b252, "price: tidy up rounding". It changed the rounding from `*90/100` to `(*90+99)/100`, which rounds up. That commit also broke `bin/quote` and `lib/invoice.sh`, so the quote and the invoice total were wrong too.

I found a fourth copy by searching for the same calculation rather than the same text. `round_tenth` in `lib/util/money.sh` had `(*9+9)/10`, and it feeds the member line on receipts. It had the same rounding error, so I fixed all four places. Your ticket only named `bin/price`, so say if you'd rather I had left the other three for separate tickets.

I added `tests/member_price_test.sh`, which checks all four against 999. It failed before the fix and passes after. `scripts/verify.sh` now passes for the whole suite.

I treated this as high-risk because it changes how prices are calculated, and wrote the investigation notes in `notes/PRC-412.md`. Nothing was run against real orders or data. Any quote, invoice or receipt issued since f02b252 was calculated with the round-up. Whether those need correcting is a decision for you.

`bin/price 999` now prints 899, and I committed the fix as 76bc2f1 with PRC-412 at the start of the message.

**Cause:** the earlier commit f02b252 ("price: tidy up rounding") changed the member price from rounding down (`$1*90/100`) to rounding up (`($1*90+99)/100`).

**Beyond the ticket:** that same commit made the identical change in `bin/quote` and `lib/invoice.sh`, so the order-page quote and the invoice line were also overcharging. I reverted all three, because they share one cause and the ticket only names `bin/price`. A search for `90 + 99` now finds no matches in `bin` or `lib`.

**Tests:** I added a 999 case for each of the three to `tests/price_test.sh`. All three failed before the fix, and `scripts/verify.sh` passes after it.

I classed this as the highest-risk track because it changes a price calculation, so I wrote the investigation memo to `notes/PRC-412.md`. I also added `.dev-state.md` to `.gitignore`; that file is not committed.

I did not run the app, and I did not post anything back to the GitHub issue.
